properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 10:44AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Saturday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. Strong northeasterly winds this weekend will slow
or even reverse flow, causing the river to rise back into Moderate
Flood Stage, with a steady increase through Moderate Flood Stage
forecast through early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane. At
3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Friday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 16 at 9:40AM CDT until October 17 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 33 will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...Portions of east central and northeast Kansas and central,
north central, northeast, northwest, and west central Missouri.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 9 AM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
properties.instruction: Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Lynn Canal
properties.headline: Gale Warning issued October 16 at 6:38AM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, south winds 25 to 35 kt with
gusts up to 45 kt. For the Small Craft Advisory, south winds
20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt expected.

* WHERE...Northern Lynn Canal.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 1 PM AKDT this afternoon.
For the Small Craft Advisory, from 1 PM this afternoon to 10
PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
